title: EFC — Is Consciousness Linked to Entropy?
description: Conceptual paper proposing that consciousness emerges at the interface between low-entropy order and high-entropy chaos sustained by continuous energy flow. It frames consciousness as an adaptive, information-efficient process in non-equilibrium systems and outlines empirical, theoretical, and artificial-system avenues to test correlations among energy flow, entropy production, and conscious function.

key_results.main_finding: Consciousness is hypothesized to arise in non-equilibrium systems where sustained energy flow maintains ordered structure while entropy provides variability, yielding maximally efficient information processing at the order–chaos interface.

sealed_predictions.statement: Across organisms and tasks, conscious states will positively correlate with both energy consumption (e.g., brain metabolic rate) and neural entropy/variability, reflecting a balance between order and randomness.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Large-scale studies showing no positive correlation (or a robust negative correlation) between validated consciousness markers and concurrent measures of metabolic rate and signal entropy after controlling for arousal, task difficulty, and anatomy.

sealed_predictions.statement: Artificial neural systems will exhibit maximal adaptability and learning at intermediate (balanced) levels of injected noise/entropy rather than at the extremes.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Benchmarks across architectures and tasks demonstrating strictly monotonic performance with noise (no interior optimum) or consistent optima at zero or maximal noise.

sealed_predictions.statement: Sustained consciousness requires continuous energy flow far from thermodynamic equilibrium.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Demonstration of sustained, reportable conscious processing in a closed, near-equilibrium system with negligible energy throughput over relevant timescales.

kill_criteria: KC1: Demonstrate sustained, reportable conscious processing in a closed, near-equilibrium system with negligible energy throughput, contradicting the need for continuous energy flow.

KC2: Show that validated neural/behavioral markers of consciousness are uncorrelated or negatively correlated with both metabolic rate and neural entropy across species and tasks after appropriate controls.

KC3: Show that modulating entropy/noise over wide ranges in biological or artificial networks leaves adaptability, learning, and consciousness-related metrics unchanged (no dependence on balance between order and randomness).

KC4: Provide robust evidence that information-processing efficiency (e.g., bits per joule, predictive coding efficiency) is systematically lower in conscious states than in matched unconscious or automated states across multiple modalities and tasks.
